workflow.description: Manifest-driven board review: context contract, blind memos, adversarial debate, EVPI expansion, regret-min stopping, MCDA synthesis, optional heterogeneous verification, deadlines, and algedonic bypass.
workflow.whenToUse: args: { question: "<decision>", board?: "{bindings}", mode?: "market-penetration", context?: "<facts>", contextData: { required fields }, debateTriggers?: [], flags?: [], namedAgentSupport?: true|false, baseline?: true }. baseline also asks one agent the question once per memo and records its plurality verdict beside the board verdict. Omit board for deterministic local classification; missing or blank required context stops before normal panel dispatch. An exact algedonic flag is the only exception and returns one immediate containment response.

phases.title: Panel
phases.detail: Blind evidence memos under a board-specific context and deliverable contract

phases.title: Challenge
phases.detail: Decision-mask challenge of the blind memos

phases.title: Synthesize
phases.detail: Locked-weight MCDA, regret stopping, and deadline handling

phases.title: Verify
phases.detail: Optional heterogeneous verification of the synthesis

phases.title: Baseline
phases.detail: Opt-in (args.baseline): one agent votes once per memo; plurality recorded beside the verdict

deliverable.shape: Per-lens evidence assessment followed by one synthesized decision

panel.brief: Strategy lens: wedge quality, positioning, sequencing, and whether this is worth roadmap or budget now. Name what would have to be true.
Pain lens: how acute and frequent is the underlying problem, who has it, what they do today, and what evidence of pull exists versus imagined demand.
Competition and prior-art lens: who solved this already, switching costs, and what a fast follower or incumbent response looks like.
Feasibility lens: build-versus-buy-versus-adopt, integration surface, hidden operational complexity, and the smallest technically honest version.
Economics lens: unit economics, cost drivers, pricing headroom, and total cost of ownership including maintenance and exit cost.
Evidence lens: existing tools, papers, or products; what a one-week spike could prove or kill; the cheapest disconfirming test.

candidates.brief: Pricing and willingness-to-pay evidence.
Data ownership, migration, and consistency risk.
Deeper competitor and alternative evidence.

panel.brief: Hidden-pain lens: recurring complaints, workarounds, switching triggers, and overlooked users.

Ignored-objection lens: the strongest bear case and evidence that would settle it.
Assumption-audit lens: rank assumptions by fragility and impact; identify the best asymmetric wedge.

triggers: adjacent users, repositioning, or timing shift

candidates.brief: Pricing and monetization evidence that could flip the opportunity.

marketing-campaign.name: Marketing campaign board
guardrails: This board runs every lens in parallel and read-only. It does not run the team's staged positioning lock; for staged drafting, launch the marketing-campaign team.
Treat the positioning lens as the lock: a finding that a channel draft contradicts the locked positioning blocks ready_for_launch and is never averaged away.
Every claim must trace to a research source or be marked unsourced. No lens publishes, sends, or changes a live account.

briefs.startup-competitive-analyst: Research lens: competitors, alternatives, and their current offers, each with a source; name the evidence gaps.
briefs.startup-review-miner: Research lens: audience language, objections, and switching triggers from reviews and support evidence, each with a source.
briefs.marketing-strategist: Positioning lens: one positioning statement and message hierarchy, each claim linked to research evidence. This is the lock the channels must carry.
briefs.startup-product-marketing-strategist: Landing-page and launch-messaging lens: whether the page and launch message carry the locked positioning, and what to change.
briefs.marketing-email-automation-lead: Email lens: sequence, triggers, and copy against the locked positioning and the offer.
briefs.marketing-paid-acquisition-strategist: Paid lens: audiences, ad angles, and spend split against the locked positioning and the offer.
briefs.marketing-creative-director: Brand review lens: voice, brand codes, and channel specs; each finding cites the positioning line it checks.
briefs.marketing-product-analytics-lead: Conversion review lens: conversion events, funnel measurement, and the test plan; each finding cites the positioning line it checks.
briefs.marketing-seo-strategist: Organic search lens, when the campaign depends on search demand.
briefs.marketing-pr-communications-lead: Earned-media lens, when the launch needs press angles or a response plan.
briefs.marketing-creative-intel-analyst: Competitor paid-creative lens from ad libraries, when paid is a main channel.

triggers: research evidence supports two or more positioning angles
a channel lens brings evidence that the locked positioning is wrong

required_sections: Evidence by file, line, or artifact

panel.brief: Architecture lens: boundaries, coupling, failure domains, and simplest design meeting the requirements.
Contract lens: API surface, versioning, compatibility, consumer migration, and future regret.
Data lens: model, ownership, consistency, migration, and query patterns.
Risk lens: 10x load, rollback, security, tenancy, and operational burden.

candidates.brief: Security and tenancy consequences that could flip the decision.
Capacity and latency evidence that could flip the decision.
Deployment and operational feasibility.
Payment-domain architecture constraints.

panel.brief: Test lens: changed-path coverage, riskiest untested scenario, flaky tests, and whether tests verify intent.
Runbook lens: deploy and rollback currency, rehearsal, on-call readiness, alerts, and dashboards.
Performance lens: latency, throughput, load evidence, regression risk, and headroom.
Rollback lens: data migrations, flags, dependency order, abort criteria, and concrete procedure.

candidates.brief: Security regression evidence.

required_sections: Evidence from logs, metrics, or traces

panel.brief: Command lens: blast radius, user impact, communications, and mitigation-versus-diagnosis in the next 30 minutes.
Diagnosis lens: hypotheses ranked by evidence and the most discriminating next test.
Signals lens: what metrics, traces, and logs show versus assumptions; telemetry blind spots.
Resilience lens: why containment failed and the cheapest recurrence guard.
Compliance lens: SOC 2 and ISO posture, truthful questionnaire answers, and audit-trail gaps.
Security lens: identity, authorization, tenancy, secrets, residency, and buyer-pentest findings.
Onboarding lens: procurement, SSO/SCIM, DPA/MSA, and where deals stall.
Operations lens: honest SLAs, support escalation, incident promises, and their cost.

candidates.brief: Privacy and governance requirements that could flip readiness.

required_sections: Assessment of the current or proposed design

panel.brief: Topology lens: agent boundaries, tool surface, state and handoff design, and the simplest topology that meets the goal.
Context lens: context budget, packet design, compression, and what the agent must never have to rediscover.
Retrieval lens: index shape, chunking, recall versus precision, freshness, and grounding failure modes.
Quality lens: eval coverage of the changed paths, observability of failures, and the cheapest disconfirming eval.

triggers: retrieval or eval tradeoffs with significant cost or UX impact

candidates.brief: Serving, deployment, and model-lifecycle constraints.

Surrounding system boundaries and integration cost.

required_sections: Evidence from queries, schemas, or metrics

panel.brief: Modeling lens: metric definitions, grain, lineage, and whether the numbers can be trusted by their consumers.
Query lens: plans, indexes, partitioning, and the cheapest change that removes the bottleneck.
Pipeline lens: delivery semantics, ordering, backfill, and late or duplicate data.
Event lens: schema quality, naming, coverage gaps, and what must be instrumented before any conclusion holds.

candidates.brief: Model ownership, consistency, and migration risk.
PII, retention, and governance constraints on the proposed change.

data-science.name: Data science and ML modelling board

required_sections: Evidence from data, backtests, or benchmarks

Temporal lens: horizon, refit cadence, rolling-origin backtest, interval coverage, and features that are not known at prediction time.
Production lens: training-serving skew, reproducibility, monitoring, and the one-command rollback path.

triggers: quantum or foundation-model pilot versus classical baseline

candidates.brief: Quantum-fit lens: classical gate, simulability, fair benchmark design, and advantage-claim status.
Metric and label definitions, grain, and lineage of the training data.
PII, consent, and retention constraints on training data and features.

panel.brief: Growth lens: where the funnel actually leaks, which loop compounds, and the single highest-leverage experiment.

Paid lens: channel economics, creative and audience levers, and CAC headroom.
Message lens: positioning, offer clarity, and content-market fit behind the numbers.

required_sections: Evidence from logs, metrics, or traces

panel.brief: Platform lens: delivery pipeline, environment shape, toil, and the simplest operating model that holds.

briefs.software-frontend-lead: Frontend delivery lens: component and state boundaries, fit with existing frontend patterns, and the delivery cost of each fix the other lenses ask for.
briefs.software-ux-designer: UX lens: flow friction, state coverage (empty, loading, error), and interaction patterns, with findings ranked by severity.
briefs.software-accessibility-reviewer: Accessibility lens: keyboard, screen-reader, contrast, and focus barriers, each mapped to a WCAG 2.2 criterion and ranked by user impact.
briefs.software-localisation-reviewer: Localisation lens: hardcoded strings, text expansion, RTL layout, and locale-aware dates, numbers, and plurals.
briefs.software-performance-reviewer: Performance lens, when the surface has a rendering, bundle-size, or Core Web Vitals risk.
briefs.software-ios-specialist: iOS lens, when the surface ships natively on iOS: HIG fit, Dynamic Type, and VoiceOver behaviour.
briefs.software-android-specialist: Android lens, when the surface ships natively on Android: Material fit, font scaling, and TalkBack behaviour.

triggers: accessibility or UX finding conflicts with frontend delivery scope
